blocks.text: Honest read

content.value: The grants/deny narrative, the timings, the proof verdicts, the B+ — all scripted constants in the deck's state machine.
Every signal the deck pretends to show already flows through the pipeline: the wish is
args.wish
; coverage accounting, run-proofs, published slice tasks, builder stamps, wave_status heartbeats, the living wave Paper, the graded debrief.
The gates. Today the lead Fable decides between phases autonomously — nothing pauses for a human, and no surface renders the run as it happens.

blocks.text: The chat technology we already have

content.value: The Studio Claude chat (epic studio-claude-chat, w1–w8 merged) is not just a chat tab — it is the substrate a live Wave Deck needs:

items.value: — spawns the host claude CLI in stream-json mode (the agent-SDK wire protocol). Admin-only by construction, hard-refused on public demo, per-host opt-out.
— chat_sessions/chat_messages; the session UUID is minted before the first byte and doubles as the
key. A wave can be a resumable session.
— pending-interaction roles already modeled and rendered:
— options plus free text, 1:1 with the deck's options-plus-note UI.
— a cross-session inbox with a strict event vocabulary (
), consumed verbatim by the S7 email notifier. “A gate is waiting on you” is a solved notification problem.
— an approved plan becomes a real published Paper, deterministic slug, idempotent (charter D49). The exact pattern for “RECORDED IN THE PAPER”.
— subagent lifecycle already parsed out of the stream and rendered. Survey dots and build bars are a re-skin of data the chat already has.

blocks.text: Pragmatic path

items.text: The static deck in docs/specs for vocabulary and choreography review — this handoff.
items.title: P0 · done

items.text: Gates + phase furniture in the regular chat. A gated arg on bp-epic-cycle asks the five gates via AskUserQuestion; choice + note project into the wave Paper; header/whisper + phase dots derive from the stream. Skill change + chat styling — no new surface.
items.title: P1 · workflow mode

items.text: A projector reads ONE finished wave (ledger + Paper + transcript) and emits scene-data JSON; the deck gets a data mode. Proves or falsifies the deck mapping for the cost of a mapper.
items.title: P2 · replay projector

items.text: The Zen deck renders the running session — a projection over the same events workflow mode already surfaces. A scene the data can't justify stays blank.
items.title: P3 · deck skin, live

items.text: Strike/add survey questions while the fleet flies: the script consults a steering channel between agent() calls. The one genuinely new mechanism — R&D, last.
items.title: P4 · in-phase steering

content.value: Real gates make waves attended by default — the countdown default-pick keeps autonomy honest rather than blocked. Scene derivation must never invent state the ledger doesn't hold. The surface is admin-only because chat transcripts are admin-gated by construction. The one-substrate law is a design gate on every slice: if it needs its own store, stream, or run loop, it's a fork — redesign it. And the deck skin waits for the replay projection — if replay looks wrong, the mapping is wrong, and we want to learn that for the price of a script.

blocks.text: Decisions to take at epic setup

items.value: Which of the five gates are real vs auto per wave, and the countdown default (seconds) for unattended runs.
Where the phase furniture lives first: Studio chat header (whisper + dots) vs CLI statusline — or both in wave 1.
The steering-channel mechanism for P4: a steering doc the script re-reads between
calls vs a live global like
Studio tab (thin plugin over the same session) ever earns its place, or the chat furniture is enough.
TUI parity: pdrender has the block set and strip law for a terminal Wave Deck later; out of scope for wave 1.
